claims.text: Dimensional scaling governs the magnetocaloric response and hysteresis of as-deposited, non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi-type nanoscale films and nanoribbons.
Dimensional scaling alters the magnetic domain structure in these alloys.
Dimensional scaling alters heat-transfer dynamics in these alloys.
Altered magnetic domain structure and heat-transfer dynamics reduce the magnetocaloric response under low applied fields.
Altered magnetic domain structure and heat-transfer dynamics increase hysteresis under low applied fields.
Reducing film thickness or nanoribbon width below 50 nm will reduce magnetocaloric response ΔS by 20% relative to a 100 nm as-deposited baseline.
Reducing film thickness or nanoribbon width below 50 nm will increase hysteresis loss HL by 30% relative to a 100 nm as-deposited baseline.
The proposed dimensional regime is 20–100 nm in film thickness or nanoribbon width.
Heat-transfer rate limits require cycle frequencies below 10 Hz.
The proposed magnetic-cooling cycles use a maximum applied field of 100 mT over 250–350 K.
Grain size, defects, and interface effects may influence the relationship between dimensional scaling and magnetocaloric response.
